consensus_findings.description: Critical: D2 requires the workspace state lock to be released across approval-service I/O (spec 'Same-generation routing is concurrency safe' -> 'approval-service waiting does not hold the workspace state lock'; task 1.4 requires an unrelated workspace transition to remain available during a blocked coordinator wait), but the decision-persistence path it routes through is a whole-file, read-modify-write of the SAME file that holds dispatch_attempts, taken from a snapshot read BEFORE the wait. `gate_router.evaluate` loads the checkpoint at gate_router.py:398, then blocks inside `service.evaluate` for the full notify_with_timeout window (approval_gate.py polls with `self.sleep` until timeout), then persists at gate_router.py:442 via `CheckpointManager.record_gate_decision` -> `save` -> `models.save_checkpoint`, which writes `checkpoint.to_dict()` wholesale (checkpoint.py:55-62, 98-123; models.py:1137-1153). Any durable transition another host task commits under `execution._state_lock` during that window (child_start's generation CAS, acknowledge, enter, a second batch's apply) is reverted when routing's decision is written; conversely, `ExecutionAdapter.apply` — which itself holds the workspace lock across the replan_required gate window at orchestrator.py:1095-1108 — will later save its own pre-route snapshot and silently drop the gate_decisions record that routing just wrote, leaving a mirror pending entry whose `decision_id` resolves to nothing and making `require_approval_ref` reject a proceed that was really granted. The reverted-claim case is durably corrupting: the attempt reverts to `prepared` while its exclusive launch marker still exists on disk, so `_write_marker_exclusive`'s O_EXCL create (execution.py:262-283) fails on every subsequent claim and the dispatch can never be re-launched. No decision, task, or test in the plan closes this: the plan adds only a gate-subject lock, which does not serialize against workspace transitions at all.

Critical: D7 and the spec scenario 'Auto posture resumes a fresh application generation' assert that clearing the generation-G `application_journal` is sufficient for the resumed generation to 'start, acknowledge, enter, and apply a fresh journal', but for any batch with more than one member that apply call cannot be made under the plan's own constraints. `resume` preserves the dispatch ID (execution.py:857-906), dispatch IDs are `{batch_id}:{item_id}:attempt-N` (orchestrator.py:320-324), and `_batch_attempts` selects every attempt with that batch prefix, so the resumed member stays in its original batch. `apply_delegated_batch` then rejects any call whose result set is not exactly the whole batch ('result membership mismatch for delegated batch', orchestrator.py:636-638), and `ExecutionAdapter.apply` is frozen unchanged by D1/the contract note, so the natural implementation — apply the resumed member's new result alone — always raises. Re-submitting the whole batch is not a safe fallback either: `execution.apply` re-runs `_validate_exact_evidence` for every success/parked member (execution.py:930-931, 961-1003), which re-resolves each sibling's worktree, branch, HEAD commit, and loop-state digest, so an already-completed sibling whose worktree was torn down, merged, or advanced after completion makes the resumed member's apply permanently unappliable. The plan's only end-to-end proof (task 1.2, test 6) is single-member, so this never surfaces in the specified test set, while task 3.4's documentation guards and task 3.1's protocol update say nothing about post-resume batch membership.

Nit: D3 makes the `escalate_resume` subject key and `_matches_subject` generation-scoped, but says nothing about the `escalate_resume` records ri-04 already wrote, which carry no `lease_generation` (the field is newly optional in the gate-decision schema). Under a generation-aware `_matches_subject`, a legacy blocked record for a currently parked dispatch no longer matches its own subject, so the first route after upgrade files and notifies a second coordinator approval for a park that is already pending, and `_apply_prior_record`'s `check_filed` reuse path is skipped for the original approval_id. D8's retirement rule compounds it: retiring 'earlier records at lower generations' has no ordering against a record with no generation, so the legacy pending mirror entry is never removed and lingers in every rehydrate and handoff.

Nit: D5 and the contract note scope the exact six-key context and the literal reason 'supervised phase retry budget exhausted' to 'an automatic policy pause', but the seam that builds that context is `gate_router.resolve_parked`, which is shared with the manual reconciliation path the proposal deliberately keeps in scope ('Sweeping policy pauses from earlier batches; those keep the existing manual reconciliation path') and which SKILL.md documents as the only sanctioned resume entry point. Today that call site passes the child-provided `parked.reason` through verbatim (gate_router.py:646). The plan never says whether the literal reason and allowlist replace it for all `policy_pause` resolutions or only route-initiated ones — so the same gate subject can be filed with two different context shapes depending on caller, and the 'no child-provided reason' privacy property does not actually hold on the retained manual path.

Optional: D1 grounds the entire safety argument — that no evaluation, notification, or resume happens before the whole batch is durable — on an unchecked caller contract ('the host calls route_parked_escalations only after apply returns successfully, which proves every batch member is terminal with application_journal.state == effects_applied'). Nothing in the plan makes `route_parked_escalations` verify that itself, and the only enforcement listed is a task 3.4 documentation guard, which asserts SKILL.md prose rather than runtime behavior. A host that calls route in an error path (exactly the shape the round-2 plan endorsed, so a plausible mis-port) would evaluate and resume members of a half-applied batch with no failure. The check is free: route already loads the named batch's attempts and `application_journal.state` is a persisted field (orchestrator.py:722-758).

The revised plan closes the complete-apply boundary defect: routing, evaluation, notification, and resume are forbidden until every named-batch member reaches terminal effects_applied, partial apply recovery replays apply through the existing journal without a second dispatch_fn call, and route failure after that boundary retries route only.

The concurrency contract is now coherent: gate_router owns a generation-aware decision-subject lock across evaluate, answer, resolve, and optional resume, while route_parked_escalations does not hold the workspace state lock across approval-service I/O and resume uses only the short state CAS.

The generation identity path is specified end to end: escalate_resume records include parked lease_generation, late-answer correlation retains it, backward-compatible gate-answer selects the newest blocked generation, explicit generation selection is supported, and require_approval_ref must reject stale-generation proceed references.

The mirror and retry semantics are now closed: later generation decisions retire older same-dispatch escalate_resume pending mirror entries, already-resumed prepared continuations are reported as already_routed with decided and resumed generations, and resumed generations clear the previous application journal before fresh apply.

The response, outbound context, work-package scope, and verification contract cover the requested surfaces: route results distinguish decided_lease_generation from resumed_lease_generation, approval context is exact and literal, cycle_state and gate-decision schema are in write scope, and validation includes supervise/recovery tests, Ruff, strict change and all-OpenSpec validation, package/DAG checks, context drift, and scope compliance.
